title: Skin a salmon fillet with a filleting knife without cutting into the flesh, and put the flesh on the plate
instruction: Skin the salmon fillet with the knife, put the flesh on the plate, and put the knife down.
context: Taking the skin off a salmon fillet is one of the commonest fish-preparation jobs in home kitchens and a routine step for food preparation workers (O*NET 35-2021.00). The edge must follow the skin-flesh boundary the whole length of the fillet while the other hand pins the skin: angled up it leaves flesh on the skin, angled down it cuts through the skin. Unlike peeling a vegetable, the blade separates two attached layers and keeps both whole.
setup: Station counter, top z = 0.7475 m; x away from the robot, y to its left. OXO Good Grips 11272900 polypropylene cutting board, 535.9 x 368.3 x 20 mm, fixed, centre (0.550, 0), top z = 0.7675. Chilled skin-on Atlantic salmon fillet portion, skin down, length along y, tail end to the left: flesh 140 x 62 mm, 11-24 mm thick (thin belly edge, thinner tail end), 164 g, centre (0.335, 0); skin 1.2 mm thick, 62 mm wide, 180 mm long, 14 g. The tail-end 40 mm of flesh was trimmed off down to the skin before the trial, leaving a 40 mm tab of bare skin beyond the flesh (y 0.070 to 0.110). Victorinox Fibrox Pro 5.3763.20 flexible filleting knife: 340 mm long, 200 mm blade (16 mm wide, 1.6 mm thick), black 140 x 30 x 23 mm handle, 85 g, lying flat on the counter right of the board, blade pointing +x, edge toward -y (it rests level on its handle; for a real trial a 10 mm block under the blade tip does the same). White 200 mm side plate (6 mm base, 10 mm rim) at (0.370, 0.310), base top z = 0.7535. Wall behind the counter at x = 0.87. Lot A: knife handle centre (0.205, -0.235, 0.759). Lot B: knife handle centre (0.215, -0.265, 0.759). Portion and plate are the same in both lots. No jitter. Screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: the salmon, skin or knife falls off the counter; the knife edge comes within 10 mm of the gripper not holding the knife by its handle, or the blade touches the gripper holding it (video); the edge cuts more than 6 mm into the flesh (ruler in the cut); the skin is cut through (any slit, held to the light; simulated as the blade pressed on the skin over 25 degrees edge-down or with over 40 N); or more than 10% of the flesh mass is left on the skin. Otherwise judged at the end, with both grippers at least 30 mm from salmon, skin and knife, each resting on the counter, board or plate, and nothing moving over 1 mm for 1 s; if not, 0. 1.0: skin completely off the flesh, flesh on the plate inside its rim, skin off the plate, at most 5% of the flesh mass left on the skin. 0.75: skin completely off but any other 1.0 condition not met (flesh not on the plate, skin on the plate, or 5-10% left on the skin). 0.5: 50-99% of the skin-flesh interface separated. 0.25: 25-49%. 0: under 25%. Real trial: ruler the separated length (or count attached area on a 5 mm grid), scrape the pink flesh off the skin and weigh it on a 0.1 g scale, top photo of the plate. Lots A and B averaged.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B) averaged
reset_notes: 1. Take a fresh chilled (0-4 C) skin-on portion; trim it to 180 x 62 mm and cut the tail-end 40 mm of flesh off down to the skin, leaving the bare tab; weigh the flesh (about 164 g). 2. Lay it skin down, tail end to the left, flesh centre at (0.335, 0) on the board. 3. Lay the knife flat on the counter at the lot's handle position, blade away from the robot, edge to the right, its tip on a 10 mm plastic block so it lies level as in the simulation. 4. Wipe the board and plate; set the plate at (0.370, 0.310). 5. In simulation each trial restores the skin bonds and resets every object to the lot's pose.
fidelity: True size. Flesh: one rigid 164 g body; skin: 1.2 mm hinged chain held on by declared bonds. PhysX cannot cut: the knife passes through flesh, rests on skin. A 5 mm cell separates when the held edge crosses it edge-first, 1 mm below to 6 mm above the skin, pressing 0.5 N or more, tab held, while a cutting resistance (estimate: 40 N/m of engaged edge against feed, 15 N/m along the blade) pushes back on the knife and forward on the skin. Edge height up to 1 mm counts as clean. Tab friction 0.9.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; both reached the 1,200-step limit; the arms moved but stayed at least 11 cm above the counter and never touched the knife, the skin tab or the salmon).
